transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Tuesday, November 17. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. Maharashtra stops work on Adani project at centre of fee-cut row. Adani Renewable Energy One Ltd has received a stop-work order for the Tarali pumped storage project in Maharashtra. The order was issued due to the absence of necessary approvals from the National Board for Wildlife. Allegations have arisen regarding the company's misrepresentation of project costs to reduce statutory obligations. Adani has stated that all required permissions and clearances were obtained before commencing work. At Sonia's book launch, Gandhis open up about love, loss, and bad chicken. Congress leader Sonia Gandhi and her family were joined by several opposition leaders at the launch event of her memoir in Delhi. The rise of Jensen Huang. The plot is both complex and simple, as if a Bhojpuri auteur had directed a John le Carré thriller: a three-part epochal tale, like the Karla Trilogy, called Saheb, Bibi, Spy, Employee aur AI. US govt proposes new rules for Green Cards; says American workers are best. The US Department of Labor is tightening regulations for companies looking to sponsor foreign workers for Green Cards. Employers will now have to demonstrate efforts to recruit qualified American candidates before hiring overseas. The introduction of new advertising techniques, such as online postings, aims to enhance job visibility. Additionally, organizations that have recently laid off US workers may face limitations on applying for PERM. 8 dead, 20 injured as bus falls into ravine in Uttarakhand. A tragic accident occurred in Tehri district, Uttarakhand, where a bus fell into a ravine. The bus was carrying approximately 30 to 35 passengers at the time of the incident. Rescue operations were launched promptly by the State Disaster Response Force teams on site. Four fatalities have been confirmed, and around 20 injured passengers are being transported to nearby hospitals. Son seeks patta for land given to mother, faces eviction; why court denied relief. A man's mother had been assigned Grama Natham land. After her death, the man continued to occupy the property and applied for the patta to be transferred in his favour as her legal heir. While his application was pending, revenue authorities initiated proceedings under the Tamil Nadu Land Encroachment Act, 1905. The Land Revenue Inspector issued a notice under Section 7, followed by a notice under Section 6 issued by the Revenue Tahsildar. Jimmy flags 'back-door takeover' of Tata Sons by Trusts, supports Chandra and listing. Breaking his silence, Jimmy Tata, Ratan Tata's younger brother, has questioned developments that, in his view, could concentrate influence within a narrower group of trustees. Watch: PM Modi visits Gurudwara Khalsa Diwan in Manila, offers prayers. Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited Gurudwara Khalsa Diwan in Manila while attending the 49th Asean Summit. He offered prayers and expressed his feelings of gratitude on social media. Several dignitaries, including senator H.E Francis Joseph Escudero, attended the visit. Established in 1901, Gurudwara Khalsa Diwan is the oldest in the Philippines and serves the Sikh community. 'Inevitable he will die in jail': Imran Khan's sons accuse Pak of torturing ex-PM. The sons of imprisoned former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan have accused authorities of subjecting their father to prolonged physical and mental torture in Adiala Jail, warning that he could die in custody without urgent medical intervention. Vance says US will not fight 'forever war' with Iran, defends Trump's military action. JD Vance emphasized that President Trump will prevent the Iran conflict from becoming a prolonged military commitment. He stated that the administration will avoid a two-year involvement despite external pressures for continued engagement. Vance defended the targeting of Iran's nuclear program, citing it as a national threat. As tensions remain high, a third US aircraft carrier has been deployed to the Middle East. Woman, granddaughter allege gold missing from locker; but commission rejects claim. A woman and her granddaughter jointly held a locker at SBI's Gunfoundry branch in Hyderabad. While the granddaughter was residing in Canada, the grandmother operated the locker in Hyderabad. The two alleged that they had deposited jewellery, pure gold coins, gold bars and melted gold weighing approximately 200 grams in the locker in 2015. They also said they had taken a photograph of the articles kept inside.
